The calendar (not the MS) is the evidence; the Haynes OCR has the same Norfolk/Suffolk/Browne letter to Hertford printed (pp. 1-2) but the OCR is too poor to tell how the two cipher lines were printed.

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE: known.py has no hit for Hatfield MS 231, Haynes or the Hertford letter; Hatfield House is not a DECODE series.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Tomokiyo's cryptiana pages do not index Henry VIII border correspondence of 1542; web search (Norfolk Hertford 1542 cipher Hatfield 231) returned only BHO calendar pages, no cipher commentary.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or DECODE item on Henry VIII border letters found (web search and known.py).
prior_art.edition: Printed twice: Haynes 1740 pp. 1-2 and calendared in LP Henry VIII 17 no. 1051; the transcriber's note says the cipher lines were not read, so neither edition gives a decipherment.
prior_art.literature: HMC Salisbury Pt I no. 79 is the calendar of the Cecil MS; the BHO cross-references for neighbouring letters (LP 1016, 1077) mention no cipher key; no study found.

vetting.key_check: No key for the Norfolk/Suffolk/Browne border-command cipher of Nov 1542 is held in the repo or known; Paget's offer to devise a cipher for Hertford (Haynes, March 1543) is a different, later exchange. Only two lines, so no statistical attack is possible even with the image.
vetting.duplicates: known.py on 'Hatfield MS 231', 'Hertford', 'Haynes' and the LP number: hits only the lead itself, research/ia_pass2_a and unrelated Oxford text; no catalogue entry or DECODE record.
